hints: Set $\tan x = \cos x \implies \sin x = \cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x$.
walkthrough:
Equate the two functions to find their intersection points:
$$\tan x = \cos x \implies \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \cos x \implies \sin x = \cos^2 x$$

Use the identity $\cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x$ to form a quadratic in $\sin x$:
$$\sin x = 1 - \sin^2 x \implies \sin^2 x + \sin x - 1 = 0$$

Solve using the quadratic formula for $\sin x$:
$$\sin x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1^2 - 4(1)(-1)}}{2} = \frac{-1 + \sqrt{5}}{2} \approx 0.618034 \quad (\text{rejecting } \approx -1.618)$$

Find the $x$-coordinate of the first intersection point $A$ (in the first quadrant $0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2}$):
$$x_A = \sin^{-1}(0.618034) \approx 0.6662 \approx 0.666\text{ radians} \quad (\text{or } 0.212\pi)$$

Point $B$ is the second intersection on $0 \le x \le \pi$ (in the second quadrant):
$$x_B = \pi - x_A = \pi - 0.666239 \approx 2.47535 \approx 2.48\text{ radians} \quad (\text{or } 0.788\pi)$$

Calculate the corresponding $y$-coordinate using $y = \cos x$:
$$y_B = \cos(2.47535) = -\cos(0.666239) = -\sqrt{1 - 0.618034^2} \approx -0.78615 \approx -0.786$$
$$\text{Coordinates of } B: \quad (2.48, -0.786)$$
